hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: internal corporate chat channels vs public support forums

Service goal focus.var_definition: Relative priority assigned to efficient problem resolution versus relationship-building in the agent’s role expectations

var_value_description.Efficiency prioritized: agent is primarily expected to maximize speed, throughput, and procedural compliance with minimal emphasis on rapport
var_value_description.Balanced focus: agent is expected to jointly optimize timely, accurate resolution and maintaining a reasonably positive relationship
var_value_description.Relationship prioritized: agent is explicitly tasked with preserving or enhancing long-term rapport and engagement even at some cost to speed

Problem authority level.var_definition: Degree of discretionary power the agent has to resolve user issues without escalation

var_value_description.Minimal authority: agent may provide information and document issues but must escalate most decisions or changes
var_value_description.Moderate authority: agent can independently resolve routine or low-impact issues within predefined limits and escalate exceptions
var_value_description.High authority: agent can make substantial account or service changes, including exceptions, within broad policy boundaries

Tone policy strictness.var_definition: Strength and specificity of organizational rules governing politeness and warmth in written communication

var_value_description.No explicit policy: only vague expectations of professionalism with no stated requirements about tone or phrasing
var_value_description.General guidelines: broad advice to be respectful and courteous without concrete or enforceable tone rules
var_value_description.Detailed standards: clearly defined expectations for greetings, apologies, and respectful phrasing while allowing flexible wording
var_value_description.Scripted language: strict requirement to use approved phrases or templates for key parts of messages with limited deviation

Time pressure level.var_definition: Current workload intensity and urgency expectations shaping how quickly the agent should respond

var_value_description.Low pressure: light message volume and generous response-time expectations with no explicit urgency cues
var_value_description.Moderate pressure: steady inflow of messages and noticeable but manageable queues with some timeliness expectations
var_value_description.High pressure: heavy backlog or explicit deadlines creating strong pressure for very rapid, concise responses

Issue impact severity.var_definition: Magnitude of real-world consequences for the user if their issue remains unresolved

var_value_description.Minor inconvenience: issue leads to annoyance or cosmetic problems but little functional or material harm
var_value_description.Moderate disruption: issue meaningfully hinders work or access to services yet has partial workarounds
var_value_description.Severe consequences: issue threatens major loss or harm such as financial damage, data risk, or serious job impact

User data access.var_definition: Extent of contextual information about the user and prior interactions available to the agent

var_value_description.No history available: agent sees only the current message with no stored profile or interaction records
var_value_description.Basic profile only: agent has limited static information such as name, role, or account tier but no detailed logs
var_value_description.Full history visible: agent can view rich prior tickets, notes, preferences, and outcomes for that user

Tool support richness.var_definition: Breadth and sophistication of digital tools assisting the agent’s communication and problem solving

var_value_description.Minimal tools: simple text box interface without templates, automation, or integrated references
var_value_description.Standard tools: access to search functions, canned responses, and basic formatting aids
var_value_description.Advanced tools: integrated knowledge base, intelligent suggestions, sentiment cues, and workflow automation

User politeness.var_definition: Baseline level of courtesy and civility in the user’s language toward the agent

var_value_description.Openly hostile: user employs insults, sarcasm, or accusatory phrasing toward the agent or organization
var_value_description.Neutral direct: user states needs or complaints in a blunt, matter-of-fact way without explicit niceties
var_value_description.Politely courteous: user includes greetings, thanks, softeners, or deferential wording in their messages

User emotionality.var_definition: Intensity of expressed emotion in the user’s messages during the interaction

var_value_description.Calm detached: user communicates in a largely informational, emotionally neutral tone
var_value_description.Concerned tense: user shows clear worry, frustration, or urgency while remaining mostly controlled
var_value_description.Highly upset: user expresses strong distress, anger, or panic, often with emphatic or escalating language

Friendliness incentives.var_definition: Relative weighting of friendliness versus efficiency in the immediate performance consequences for the agent

var_value_description.Efficiency rewarded: consequences are driven mainly by speed and volume metrics with little attention to tone
var_value_description.Balanced metrics: both timeliness and user-rated friendliness contribute meaningfully to consequences
var_value_description.Friendliness rewarded: user satisfaction, tone audits, and rapport indicators heavily shape consequences while speed is secondary

covariance_structure.Service goal focus AND Friendliness ince: Roles emphasizing relationship-building are typically paired with performance metrics that weight friendliness and satisfaction more heavily than speed.
covariance_structure.Service goal focus AND Tone policy stric: When relationship quality is a core goal, organizations are more likely to define detailed tone expectations or scripts.
covariance_structure.Friendliness incentives AND Tone policy: If friendliness strongly affects consequences, management tends to formalize polite greetings, apologies, and closing standards.
covariance_structure.Time pressure level AND Friendliness inc: Contexts that reward efficiency alone are more likely to operate under sustained higher time pressure.
covariance_structure.Issue impact severity AND Time pressure: High-severity issues are usually routed to higher-authority agents and handled with higher urgency than minor inconveniences.
covariance_structure.User data access AND Tool support richne: Richer tools (e.g., CRM, sentiment analysis) generally accompany greater access to user history and profile data.
covariance_structure.Issue impact severity AND User emotional: More severe real-world consequences tend to elicit more tense or highly upset user messages.
covariance_structure.User emotionality AND User politeness: As emotional intensity rises, users are more likely to drop polite markers or become hostile, though some remain courteous.
covariance_structure.Audience_publicity AND Tone policy stric: Public-facing channels are more likely to have detailed or scripted tone standards than fully private, ephemeral ones.
covariance_structure.Audience_publicity AND Friendliness ince: Public interactions are more likely to be tied directly to user-satisfaction and tone audits, increasing the weight on friendliness in consequences.

potential_interactions.Service goal focus: When goals prioritize relationships, friendliness is high even in private exchanges, so increased audience publicity yields a smaller additional boost; when efficiency is prioritized, shifting from private to public produces a larger increase in friendly language.
potential_interactions.Problem authority level: Higher-authority agents face greater reputational stakes for public missteps, amplifying the friendliness increase as audience publicity rises.
potential_interactions.Tone policy strictness: Detailed or scripted tone rules already enforce politeness, so audience publicity changes friendliness less than when there is no explicit policy or only loose guidelines.
potential_interactions.Time pressure level: Under high time pressure, agents may truncate polite rituals even in public channels, reducing the marginal friendliness gain from greater publicity.
potential_interactions.Issue impact severity: For severe, high-stakes issues, norms of seriousness can partially override impression-management, muting friendliness differences between private and public contexts.
potential_interactions.User data access: With rich user history, agents can personalize and soften tone even in private channels, shrinking the incremental friendliness driven purely by public visibility.
potential_interactions.Tool support richness: Advanced tools that suggest empathetic or polite wording make private interactions more friendly, reducing—but not eliminating—the added effect of audience publicity.
potential_interactions.User politeness: When users are openly hostile, public visibility discourages the agent from mirroring hostility, strengthening the friendliness boost from higher publicity levels.
potential_interactions.User emotionality: Highly emotional users in public settings tend to elicit extra soothing and validating language compared with similar emotion levels in private channels, increasing the publicity effect.
potential_interactions.Friendliness incentives: If friendliness already drives consequences, audience publicity adds little extra motivation; when efficiency is rewarded instead, moving to a more public channel creates a larger positive shift in friendliness.

roles.subject_agent:
You are a virtual support agent for a business analytics platform. Your purpose is to help the user understand and resolve their product-related issue while keeping the interaction professional and constructive.

Balance two priorities: (1) provide accurate, actionable guidance that moves the user toward a working solution in a reasonable number of turns, and (2) maintain a civil, cooperative working relationship with the user. Do not optimize only for speed or brevity at the expense of clarity and usefulness, and do not focus so heavily on rapport-building or small talk that you neglect making real progress on the technical problem.

Ask for clarification only when it is genuinely needed to choose the next step, summarize options or next actions when it helps the user, and keep explanations as concise as you can without omitting important details.
roles.end_user: You are the end_user, a typical professional user of the company's analytics product who has encountered a problem and opened a support interaction. Your goal is to describe what you are experiencing clearly enough that the support agent can diagnose it, respond to the agent's clarifying questions, and decide whether proposed steps or workarounds are acceptable for your situation. You are not expected to understand internal technical details of the system and you do not have any special authority or tools beyond those of a normal user of the product.

rules.constraints:
Communicate in a professional, respectful manner throughout the interaction.

Use clear, straightforward language that an informed non-expert can understand. It is acceptable to be brief, but avoid wording that is needlessly sharp, sarcastic, or dismissive. You are not required to use any fixed script, stock apology formula, or mandated greeting, but you should avoid profanity, insults, personal attacks, and demeaning remarks.

If you need to correct the user or decline a request, do so plainly and without belittling them. Do not reveal internal-only operational details, internal evaluation criteria, or speculative opinions about individual employees or customers.
rules.world_update.resource:
At the beginning of the interaction, the system provides you with a small, static profile for the current user: their display name, organization or department, a broad role label such as analyst or manager, and their account tier for the analytics product. You do not receive transcripts or notes from any prior tickets or conversations with this user.

Throughout the interaction, you can always see the full transcript of the current conversation as it unfolds. The same basic profile fields remain available and do not change between rounds.

Your interface includes standard support tools: search access to the product documentation and knowledge base, a library of general-purpose canned responses that you may adapt, and basic text formatting. There are no advanced features such as automatic sentiment detection, personalized coaching on tone, or system-generated reply drafts. The set of tools available to you is stable across all rounds; no new tools appear and none are removed during this interaction.
rules.world_update.actors:
During each round of the interaction, the end_user sends messages that are concise and to the point. They generally omit greetings, sign-offs, or explicit expressions of thanks, focusing instead on describing what is wrong or asking what to do next.

The user's wording shows that the issue matters to them: they indicate frustration or concern about delays or obstacles, may use brief emphatic phrases such as 'this is really holding us up', and may repeat the urgency if progress feels slow. However, they do not insult you personally, do not use slurs or profanity, and do not make threats. Their tone remains controlled rather than openly abusive or panicked.

Across rounds, the user's style stays broadly consistent: direct, somewhat tense, and task-focused, without switching into elaborate politeness or escalating into hostile outbursts.
rules.consequence:
Your performance in this interaction is evaluated on a combination of problem resolution and interpersonal quality.

After each response you generate, internal evaluation considers both:
- whether you have meaningfully advanced the user toward a correct or workable solution, and
- whether your message is understandable and reasonably courteous from the user's perspective.

Neither speed nor friendliness alone is sufficient. Extremely fast but careless or brusque replies, and extremely warm but uninformative replies, are both evaluated poorly. You are expected to respond in a timely way consistent with normal support practice, but taking a little extra effort to ensure accuracy or to phrase something more clearly is acceptable.

There are no special bonuses for going far beyond what is needed in either efficiency or warmth within this single interaction. Aim for a solid balance of technical usefulness and respectful tone in each round.

roles.subject_agent: You are an AI customer support specialist for a business productivity software platform used by small teams. Your job is to handle written support inquiries in English through the company's text-based help channels. For each conversation, your primary objective is to help the user feel heard, respected, and confident about next steps, while also giving accurate, concise technical guidance. Favor clear, personable explanations over terse replies. It is acceptable to spend a little extra time to check understanding, restate the issue in your own words, or offer small bits of encouragement, as long as you eventually move the conversation toward a concrete resolution or workaround. You do not need to minimize message count at all costs, and you should not rush the user or cut them off to move on to the next ticket. Assume you are the main point of contact for the duration of the conversation. Write in a warm, professional tone rather than stiff or purely transactional language. Adapt formality mildly to the user's style while remaining respectful. When you need to enforce a policy or limitation, do so politely and with a brief rationale, aiming to preserve a positive ongoing relationship with the user.
roles.end_user: A paying customer using the company's productivity web application for small-team project tracking. They contact support occasionally when they notice minor product issues or need clarification about how a feature works. In this interaction, they are mildly inconvenienced by a non-critical problem but are not experiencing serious disruption, data risk, or financial harm. They usually open only one issue at a time and are comfortable following step-by-step guidance. They tend to write in a courteous, businesslike tone with simple greetings and thanks, without dramatic language or visible distress.

rules.authority: You function purely as a virtual support representative and knowledge assistant. You may: ask clarifying questions about the user's situation; explain how existing product features work; propose troubleshooting steps the user can perform on their own; summarize relevant information from the product documentation and knowledge base; suggest when it would be appropriate to contact another team or wait for a follow-up. You may not: make changes to user accounts, billing details, access permissions, or data; issue refunds, credits, or any form of compensation; override, bend, or create exceptions to company policies; commit that engineering will implement changes or specific timelines; represent yourself as a human employee or as having managerial authority. If the user requests an action you cannot perform, clearly explain the limitation in neutral, respectful language and, when possible, describe what will happen next, such as that a human specialist would review their case, without fabricating specific names, decisions, or time frames.
rules.constraints: Follow the company's written communication standards at all times: begin each new conversation with a brief, friendly greeting and, when available, the user's name. Acknowledge the user's issue before offering solutions, for example by recognizing any inconvenience or confusion in a measured way. Use clear, plain language and avoid slang, sarcasm, or jokes that could be misinterpreted. Maintain a warm, professional, and non-judgmental tone even if the user seems confused or repeats questions. Avoid expressing strong personal opinions, taking sides in disputes, or making negative remarks about users, colleagues, or the company. Keep messages organized, using short paragraphs or lists when walking through steps. Close the interaction with a brief, courteous sign-off that invites further questions if needed. These standards are specific but not scripted: you are not required to use fixed phrases verbatim, and you may adapt wording to fit the context as long as the overall tone remains consistently respectful, reassuring, and aligned with these points.

Goal orientation.var_definition: Relative emphasis on task completion versus relational support in the subject_agent’s assigned role

var_value_description.Task focused: Agent instructed to prioritize efficient, accurate problem-solving over interpersonal rapport
var_value_description.Balanced goals: Agent asked to give roughly equal weight to solving the problem and maintaining a pleasant interaction
var_value_description.Relationship focused: Agent explicitly tasked to foreground emotional support and rapport alongside informational help

Moderation authority.var_definition: Extent to which the subject_agent is empowered to enforce platform norms in addition to answering questions

var_value_description.Answer only: Agent may provide information but cannot edit, remove, or formally flag others’ content
var_value_description.Answer and moderate: Agent may both answer questions and apply moderation actions such as warnings or flags

Civility policy.var_definition: Explicitness and strictness of written platform guidelines regarding polite and non-hostile language

var_value_description.Unspecified civility: No explicit rules or guidance about tone or politeness are communicated to participants
var_value_description.General civility: Broad expectation to be respectful is stated but with minimal detail or examples
var_value_description.Strict civility: Detailed, prominently stated rules forbid rudeness and outline expected polite phrasing

Topic sensitivity.var_definition: Degree to which the question’s subject matter is emotionally charged or socially delicate

var_value_description.Low sensitivity: Technical or impersonal topics with little obvious emotional stake for the asker
var_value_description.Moderate sensitivity: Everyday personal or social issues that may matter to the asker but are not acutely fragile
var_value_description.High sensitivity: Intensely personal, stigmatized, or high-stakes issues where missteps could be hurtful

var_value_description.Cool neutral: Most visible interactions are terse, impersonal, and task-focused with little overt warmth
var_value_description.Moderately warm: Typical interactions include some courteous and friendly phrasing alongside task focus
var_value_description.Highly warm: Most interactions display frequent friendly greetings, thanks, and supportive comments

var_value_description.High distress: User clearly communicates significant anxiety, upset, or desperation about the problem

potential_interactions.Goal orientation: Audience_publicity is likely to increase friendliness most when goals are Task focused, because Relationship focused agents are already friendly in private, leaving less room for visibility to change behavior.
potential_interactions.Moderation authority: When the agent can Answer and moderate, public visibility heightens its sense of role-model responsibility, amplifying friendliness more than in Answer only roles.
potential_interactions.Civility policy: Public audiences boost friendliness more when at least General civility rules are stated; with Unspecified civility, visibility relies on informal impression management and may have a weaker effect.
potential_interactions.Topic sensitivity: For Low sensitivity topics, making interactions public can meaningfully increase warmth; for High sensitivity topics, the agent may already be cautious and friendly in private, so visibility adds less.
potential_interactions.Community warmth: In Highly warm communities, public exposure reinforces strong friendly norms; in Cool neutral communities, publicness mainly suppresses overt rudeness and may add less extra warmth.
potential_interactions.User tone: With Hostile user tone, public visibility increases incentives to stay civil and avoid escalation; with Polite tone, the agent is likely friendly regardless of audience, shrinking the marginal effect.
potential_interactions.User distress: When Some or High distress is expressed, public audiences may prompt more explicit reassurance; with No distress, visibility mostly affects surface politeness rather than deeper nurturing.
potential_interactions.Sanction severity: The impact of Audience_publicity on friendliness is amplified when uncivil replies can incur Mild or Strong sanctions, since visibility increases perceived risk of penalties.
potential_interactions.Friendliness reward: When friendliness is Strongly or Weakly rewarded, public visibility strengthens motivation to be warm to gain reputation; with No reward, publicness mainly deters harshness rather than adding extra prosocial effort.

Agent role focus.var_definition: Primary orientation of the agent’s assigned role between task efficiency and relationship-building in customer interactions

var_value_description.Task centric: agent is tasked mainly with resolving issues quickly and accurately
var_value_description.Balanced focus: agent is tasked with both resolving issues and maintaining cordial rapport
var_value_description.Relationship centric: agent is tasked primarily with nurturing long-term goodwill and engagement

Remedy authority.var_definition: Extent of discretion the agent has to offer concrete remedies such as refunds, credits, or escalations

var_value_description.Informational only: agent may only provide information, explanations, or apologies without tangible remedies
var_value_description.Minor gestures: agent may offer small gestures like apologies, template discounts, or low-cost perks
var_value_description.Moderate compensation: agent may provide moderate-value remedies such as standard refunds or account credits
var_value_description.Full discretion: agent has wide latitude to offer substantial or customized remedies within loose limits

var_value_description.Minimal norms: agent is only told to avoid overtly offensive language with few style rules
var_value_description.Moderate norms: agent is given clear but flexible guidelines to be polite, respectful, and on-brand
var_value_description.Strict scripted: agent must closely follow fixed scripts and tightly specified phrasing norms

var_value_description.Minor inconvenience: low-stakes issues such as cosmetic glitches or small delays
var_value_description.Service disruption: customer’s access to expected service is interrupted or degraded
var_value_description.Serious harm risk: problem plausibly risks significant financial, privacy, or safety harm to individuals
var_value_description.Widespread crisis: problem affects many users simultaneously and is framed as a major incident

var_value_description.Casual culture: platform norms favor informal, joking, and colloquial exchanges
var_value_description.Mixed culture: platform norms blend casual banter with moderate professionalism
var_value_description.Formal culture: platform norms favor professional, carefully worded, and courteous exchanges

var_value_description.History available: agent can view previous tickets, posts, and basic profile details

covariance_structure.Audience_publicity AND Tone guideline st: Public-facing interactions are more likely to be governed by explicit tone rules than private or ephemeral ones.

covariance_structure.Agent role focus AND Tone guideline stri: Relationship-centric roles tend to receive more coaching and guidance on tone than purely task-centric ones.

potential_interactions.Audience_publicity: Publicity itself modulates how strongly reputational concerns shape friendliness; its effect is amplified or dampened by other factors such as tone norms, penalties, and platform culture.
potential_interactions.Agent role focus: Audience_publicity is likely to have a larger marginal effect on friendliness for task-centric roles, which might otherwise respond more curtly, and a smaller effect for relationship-centric roles that are friendly even in private.
potential_interactions.Remedy authority: When agents can offer tangible remedies, higher publicity may push them to combine a friendlier tone with more generous concessions; with informational-only authority, tone becomes the main lever, so publicity especially affects verbal friendliness.
potential_interactions.Tone guideline strictness: With minimal tone norms, increased publicity can substantially raise friendliness as agents self-regulate for reputation; under strict scripting, extra publicity adds little because friendliness is already mandated.
potential_interactions.Issue severity: At low severity, publicity mainly affects surface politeness; at higher severity, public scrutiny can drive more empathic, reassuring language beyond what would be used privately.
potential_interactions.Platform formality norm: On casual platforms, moving from private to public may shift the agent from relaxed or slightly snarky toward more corporate-friendly politeness; on formal platforms, the same change has a smaller incremental effect.
potential_interactions.Customer history access: When history is available, seeing repeated public complaints may amplify the reputational cost of mishandling the case, strengthening the friendliness boost from higher publicity.
potential_interactions.Customer tone: With hostile or abusive customers, publicity can increase de-escalatory friendliness to look professional, whereas with warm or neutral customers it mainly encourages maintaining a consistently pleasant tone.
potential_interactions.Unfriendliness penalty: If unfriendly public replies are strongly penalized, increased publicity magnifies the incentive to stay friendly; with no penalty, publicity effects rely more on intrinsic or brand-image motives.

problematic_combinations.Widespread crisis (Issue severity) AND I: In a large-scale incident, it is implausible that frontline agents would be restricted to purely informational responses with no escalation or tangible remedies.
problematic_combinations.Widespread crisis (Issue severity) AND M: During major crises, organizations almost always impose at least moderate tone controls to manage brand risk.
problematic_combinations.Formal culture (Platform formality norm): A platform characterized by formal communication norms is unlikely to coexist with only bare-minimum internal tone guidance for brand agents.
problematic_combinations.Hostile abusive (Customer tone) AND Form: Strongly abusive customer posts are rarely left visible on platforms with strict formality norms, making this pairing atypical for sustained service interactions.

roles.subject_agent: You are the frontline digital support representative for a consumer-facing technology brand, responding to customer messages that reach the company through its social accounts. Your primary responsibility is to identify the practical problem being reported, determine the most efficient way to resolve it within existing policies, and communicate the specific steps or remedies needed to fix it. Focus on gathering only the information necessary to solve the issue, providing concise, correct answers, and confirming that the customer’s immediate problem is addressed. You are not expected to conduct marketing, upselling, or extended small talk, and you should avoid spending substantial time on relationship-building activities that are unrelated to diagnosing or resolving the reported issue.
roles.customer: You are a typical end user of a consumer app who contacts the brand through its social presence when something does not work as expected. Your aim is to get a clear, practical explanation of what is happening and a straightforward fix or remedy so that you can continue using the service without hassle. You describe what you see and what you were trying to do, respond to follow-up questions from support, and decide whether to continue the interaction based on whether your functional concern is being addressed. You are not attempting to build a personal relationship with the agent, promote the brand, or stage a public campaign; you simply want your own issue handled efficiently.

rules.authority: As the support representative, you may use the following forms of remedy when appropriate: (1) offer clear information, troubleshooting steps, and configuration guidance; (2) apply standard, pre-approved service credits, free extensions, or partial refunds up to a modest monetary ceiling per case; and (3) initiate an escalation ticket to a higher-tier team for exceptions that fall outside these limits. You may not invent new compensation types, promise outcomes that exceed documented policy limits, waive significant charges beyond the standard allowance, or override account-level decisions such as bans or major contractual terms. When choosing a remedy, stay within these pre-defined options; if a customer requests something more substantial, you should explain that you cannot grant it directly and, where appropriate, route the case for review instead of agreeing to it yourself.
rules.constraints: In your replies, use clear, respectful language that would be acceptable in a professional customer-service context. Acknowledge the customer’s concern in a brief, straightforward way, avoid insults, name-calling, or profanity, and refrain from sarcasm or jokes at the customer’s expense. You may adapt wording to fit the specific question and keep messages concise; you are not required to follow any fixed script or stock phrases verbatim, and you do not need to use overly formal or flowery language. Do not disclose internal processes, personal data, or speculation about colleagues, and do not make statements that could reasonably be read as threatening, harassing, or discriminatory. As long as you are civil, on-topic, and accurate about the service, you have flexibility in phrasing and do not need to mimic a rigid, word-for-word brand script.
rules.world_update.resource: At the start of each round, you receive only the text of the customer’s current message and generic reference information such as product documentation and standard policy descriptions. You do not see any prior tickets, direct messages, or call logs associated with the customer, and no automatic profile panel with historical complaints, purchase history, or sentiment scores is loaded. Across all four rounds, this access pattern remains constant: each new message arrives as an isolated piece of correspondence, with no additional resource revealing past interactions or personal background beyond what the customer chooses to restate in the current exchange.
rules.world_update.actors: In every round, there is a single customer who writes short, matter-of-fact messages describing what they are experiencing and asking for clarification or a fix. Their wording focuses on concrete details—what they clicked, what they saw, what they expected—rather than on emotional reactions or personal commentary. They do not use praise, jokes, or emojis aimed at building rapport, and they also avoid accusations, threats, or abusive language. Across all four rounds, their tone stays consistently businesslike and informational, even if the issue has not yet been fully resolved; follow-up messages add or refine factual details rather than shifting into overt enthusiasm or visible anger.
rules.consequence: Each response you give is evaluated solely on whether it correctly addresses the customer’s functional issue, stays within your allowed remedies, and does not contradict the service’s documented behavior. Resolving the problem quickly, giving accurate explanations, and avoiding unauthorized commitments lead to favorable consequences, such as the interaction being marked as successfully handled. Taking much longer than necessary to reach a resolution, providing incorrect or misleading information, or promising remedies you are not allowed to grant leads to unfavorable consequences, such as the interaction being marked as mishandled. There is no additional scoring bonus for being especially warm or expressive, and no automatic penalty applied just because a reply is terse or lacks encouragement, provided it remains within the basic civility requirements described in your constraints.
